title: Accuracy in Predicting Repetitions to Task Failure in Resistance Exercise: A Scoping Review and Exploratory Meta-analysis
population: 12 studies with 414 healthy participants who predicted repetitions to failure in a set taken to failure.
key_findings: On average, people underpredicted the repetitions they had left before failure by about one repetition (0.95, interval 0.17 to 1.73), with very large variation between studies.
Predictions were somewhat more accurate when made closer to failure, in sets with 12 or fewer repetitions to failure, and slightly in later sets.
Training experience did not appear to change accuracy, and upper and lower body exercises did not clearly differ.
methods: Scoping review with an exploratory multilevel meta-analysis and meta-regressions of prediction error.
limitations: Extreme heterogeneity (I² 97.9%); studies explained and confirmed failure differently; the authors leave open whether the observed error is acceptable.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
